To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absorption properties of the composites can be tuned by the wire geometry, mesostructure, wire orientation, and wire concentration.
the absorption performance of GFRP laminated composites can be enhanced by adding microwires, which are aligned in the fiber direction and distributed in the form of random pattern.
the microwave absorption performance of structural composites can be tuned by adjusting the local properties of ferromagnetic micowires.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, fabrication and characterization of a new class of GFRP composites for microwave absorption applications, which may provide a new insight for the development of microwave absorbing materials.
the microwave absorption of GFRP laminated composite materials containing ferromagnetic glass coated microwires.

the design and optimization of the GFRP composites with ferromagnetic microwsires for microwave absorption applications, which may provide a new route for developing the next generation of microwave absorbers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microwave absorption properties of the GFRP composites containing ferromagnetic microribbons or amorphous microwires are strongly dependent on the local structure of the wires.
the microwave absorption performance of the GFRP laminated composite containing microwire is determined by the local wire structure and its interaction with the glass fiber structure.

, for the unidirectionally reinforced GFRP laminated composites, the absorption is mainly dominated by the wire geometry, the orientation and the concentration of wires, and the mesostructure of the wire system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GFRP with ferromagnetic wires is a new kind of composite materials for microwave absorbers.

the absorption is dominated by the wires and the mesoscopic structures of the wires, and the absorption of the GFRP is determined by the wires, the mesoscopic structures and the orientation of the wires, the number of laminated composites, and the polarization effect.

the microwave absorption of GFRP composites containing ferromagnetic wires is a result of the interplay of the local properties of microwires, the mesoscopic properties of wires, the properties of the polymer matrix and the properties of glass fibers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microwave absorption properties of the composites can be tailored by adjusting the local structure of the microwires.
the absorption performance of GFRP laminated composites can be tailored by controlling the local properties of microwires.
the microwave absorption of structural composites can be tuned through the local properties of the wires, and this is of significance for the design of structural composites for microwave absorption.
